summary:
Found while designing #4753's live lock controls on 2026-10-30.

- **The mechanism:** FS.GG.Rendering and FS.GG.Game `release.yml` both declare `concurrency: group: release-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. GitHub serializes runs in the same group, meaning the same repository and the same ref, before any job starts. Under that setting it keeps only one pending run, so a further dispatch can replace the pending one. Two runs on the same repository and ref therefore never meet at the ADR-0097 org-wide publication-writer lock (`scripts/publication_writer_lock.py`).
- **Why it matters:** the only live lock sample is the four acquisitions in the FS.GG.UI 0.32.4 journey, all on 2026-10-30. Per #4753's reconciliation comment, each showed 0 other live participants and waited only the 30 s floor (`SETTLE_SECONDS` 20 + `CONFIRM_SECONDS` 10). That shows the floor cost, not fencing.
- **How to apply:** to demonstrate lock queueing live, use publisher jobs in different concurrency groups, for example two repositories, or different refs or events in one repository. The wait appears only in step logs (`publication lock: waiting for N older publisher job(s)`) and in the receipt's `waitedSeconds` / `otherLiveParticipants`. Do not treat a green uncontended publication as evidence of fencing.
- **Limits:** the group mechanism comes from reading the cited workflows. The pending-run replacement is documented GitHub behavior, not observed here. The acquisition figures come from 0.32.4 run logs and receipts, summarized on #4753 (comment 6518549798), not from source. Runs on different refs or triggering events of the same repository (tags, release, branch dispatches) fall in different groups and can reach the lock concurrently; this record does not cover them. The live cross-repo control outcome is recorded on #4753.
title: Same-ref release concurrency groups queue runs before the org publication-writer lock, so same-ref contention never exercises it
